title: Console MVP reprioritization: focused cuts for cost breakdown, tracing, and dashboards
creator: Sofia Chen
description: This ticket documents a targeted scope reduction for the Redwood Console observability surface to hit a reliable MVP for the March release. We need to ship a minimal set of dashboards, an initial tracing surface, and a pared-down cost breakdown that deliver immediate value to customers while deferring lower-impact features.
background: Multiple stakeholder reviews concluded that the original console observability scope is too broad for the March ship window. Engineering constraint: runtime telemetry schema work (ENG-8812) and tracing ingestion pipeline (ENG-9021) are partial. PMs and Design aligned on prioritizing visibility that prevents customer outages and surfaces cost hotspots over deep exploratory tooling.
scope_included: Core dashboards: 4 cards (overall throughput, 95th latency by route, error rate by route, active model usage)
Simplified cost breakdown: aggregate token spend by model and by route (7-day and 30-day windows), CSV export for top-level view
Tracing: sampled traces at 1% for production routes, basic flamegraph/time-series view with search by request id
Rollouts & alerts: attach cost spike and SLO breach alerts to routes (email + console notification), basic runbook link
Console UX: filter by time range and region, short contextual help copy
scope_removed: Per-token-level cost attribution for nested tooling (defer to next milestone)
Full distributed trace correlator (deferred advanced trace correlator and inferred causality)
User-configurable trace sampling UI (default to 1% per route for MVP)
Heatmap widgets and ad-hoc query editor
Expanded export formats (only CSV provided for MVP)
Retention beyond 30 days for trace payloads (defer longer retention to Dedicated customers)
Per-token cost breakdown in dashboard cards (show model-route aggregates only)
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: 4 specified cards render within 1.2s on first load with a cold cache in staging environment
Dashboards: date-range and region filters return results consistent with query latencies observed in backend metrics (difference < 5%)
Cost breakdown: aggregated spend by model and by route for last 7 and 30 days displays and CSV export contains matching totals to billing dataset (reconcile script included)
Tracing: sampled production traces are visible in the UI for sampled requests; searching by request id returns the full captured span tree within 2s
Alerts: cost spike alert triggers in staging when synthetic traffic increases token consumption by 50% over baseline and alert arrives to configured email
Security: console surfaces no sensitive request payloads in tracing view (only metadata and spans), verified by security review checklist
Documentation: PRD and acceptance criteria published in Confluence and linked from ticket; Design handoff (Figma) completed and reviewed
E2E: QA test plan executed with pass rate >= 95% on the acceptance cases listed in this ticket
rollout_plan: Canary: enable console dashboards and tracing for 10% of internal accounts for 48 hours
Monitoring: run synthetic checks for dashboard freshness and trace ingestion during canary
Rollout: increase to 50% for 24 hours if no critical issues, then full rollout
Fallback: quick rollback to previous console build and disable trace ingestion if errors exceed threshold (error rate > 2% of console requests)
Post-launch: collect feedback via support channel and schedule a 1-week triage cadence
open_questions: Do enterprise customers require >30 day retention for traces by contract? (legal/sales to confirm)
Should we expose sampling rate toggle to select customers in Dedicated mode (defer decision to Dedicated product path)
Are there any additional billing reconciliation fields required for finance before GA?
What exact runbook link should be attached to SLO alerts (ops to provide)
Validate whether CSV export needs anonymized IDs for HIPAA/Sensitive customers
